answer: Sybil defense via live liveness lotteries: the network randomly summons identities to complete short puzzles in a tight window — a zephyr of challenges, not a scheduled exam. One operator cannot answer for many fakes at once, since each puzzle demands real-time attention; fakes summoned together fail together. Summons are unpredictable, so attackers cannot pre-compute answers or rotate a crew through them. Missed summons decay standing; repeated misses revoke it. Honest agents pass easily — but an ocean of fakes means being everywhere at once, and no attacker can stand on every ridge.
